$optimize¶

Geometry optimization, saddle-point search, IRC and relaxed scans.

Relevant when: task = optimize | optimize+hessian | irc | scan | opt_n1

saddle¶

Type: switch
Default: 0
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, Dft.rtf, chemport.ru forum, qchem.ru forum

Type of stationary point sought.

Value

Meaning

0

Optimize to a minimum. (default)

1

Optimize to a saddle point.

Note

A saddle-point search needs an accurate Hessian in the input: compute one with task=hessian and append its $Energy block (the eng> lines). A usual route is scan → Hessian at the scan maximum → saddle=1 → task=hessian to confirm one imaginary frequency → IRC. In version 25 the output confirms the search with Saddle point search: follow = 1 and, when a Hessian was read from $Energy, Lowest eigenvalues: with one negative value.

See also: follow ($optimize), H ($Energy)

tolerance¶

Type: list
Default: 0.0001,0.01
Units: au
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, official site files, input.txt

Convergence tolerance on the gradient (first value) and on the displacement (second value).

About the default: if only the first value is given, the second is 100 times larger (the recommended setting).

See also: accuracy ($grid)

trust¶

Type: list
Default: 0.125,0.015625
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, official site files, input.txt, Dft.rtf, chemport.ru forum

Trust radius (the largest allowed step), given as maximum, minimum and initial values.

About the default: echoed by version 25 as Trust radius = 0.12500000 (max), 0.01562500 (min) in internal coordinates, with symmetry (sym=1) and with cartesian=1. v13 and v15 echoed 0.2 / 0.0125 in internal coordinates and 0.1 / 0.00625 with cartesian=1; v6 echoed 0.2 / 0.0125 in Cartesian coordinates. Dft.rtf gives 0.5 (older version). input.txt says that if only the maximum is given, the minimum is 1/16 of it and the initial value 1/4. Version 25 uses 1/8 instead: trust=0.2 alone was echoed as 0.20000000 (max), 0.02500000 (min).

follow¶

Type: integer
Default: 1
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, Dft.rtf

Follow the n-th Hessian eigenvector in a saddle-point search.

About the default: 1 according to Dft.rtf; version 25 echoes Saddle point search: follow = 1.

See also: saddle ($optimize)

steps¶

Type: integer
Default: 128
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, Dft.rtf, qchem.ru forum

Maximum number of optimization cycles.

Note

Version 25 echoes Maximum number of steps = 128 when steps is not given; older sources give 50. When the limit is reached the program prints no message: the output just ends, and the last geometry appears only in mol> lines, not MOL>. Dft.rtf warns that an optimization not converged after about 50 steps very likely has something wrong with it, and that computing a Hessian first helps in many cases; so don’t simply raise steps. In v6, if both steps and step are given, the value of step is used; give only one of them.

See also: tolerance ($optimize), steps ($d2edr2)

cartesian¶

Type: switch
Default: 0
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, official site files, input.txt, chemport.ru forum

Coordinate system for the optimization. The output reports Coordinates: internal or cartesian.

Value

Meaning

0

Redundant internal coordinates. (default)

1

Cartesian coordinates (last resort).

Note

cartesian=1 is the fix when the program crashes with process 0 got signal 6 after a too few message in the internal-coordinate table. In version 25, bent CO2 and acetylene that became linear during the optimization converged in internal coordinates without that crash (the number of internal coordinates dropped instead), and also with cartesian=1.

back¶

Type: switch
Default: 0
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, chemport.ru forum, LIMOR page

IRC direction. A full IRC takes two runs, one per direction: version 25 with the default back=0 followed one direction only (n = 1, back = 0, down = 1 in the output), and back=1 the other one (negative distance values on the IRC> lines). Re-optimize the endpoints afterwards, because an IRC does not end at a converged minimum.

Value

Meaning

0

Trace the IRC path forwards. (default)

1

Trace the IRC path backwards.

See also: points ($optimize), radius ($optimize)

points¶

Type: integer
Default: none stated
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt

Number of points to optimize in an IRC run, or number of constrained geometry optimizations in a scan run. In a scan the points include both ends: points=4 gives s = 0, 1/3, 2/3 and 1. An IRC can stop before points is reached when it arrives at a minimum.

See also: value ($optimize)

radius¶

Type: real
Default: 0.1
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, Dft.rtf, chemport.ru forum

Radius, in mass-weighted coordinates, for IRC path optimization. Adjacent IRC points end up roughly twice this distance apart. The IRC coordinate is reported in bohr·amu^1/2.

About the default: 0.1 as echoed by version 25 (r = 0.1000000000); Dft.rtf gives 0.2 (older version).

Note

Vicinity of a Stationary Point(?) --- STOP. ends an IRC that has reached the region of a minimum; in version 25 it was the normal end of a test IRC. Users have also seen it early, when the energy did not decrease on a step; changing the step size is the reported fix there. The other normal end is Energy Minimum Passed --- STOP., printed after a point that came out higher than the one before; in version 25 it sometimes followed the Vicinity message. In a version 25 IRC of HCN ⇄ HNC, radius=0.03 and 0.1 reached both minima (about 65 and 20 points per direction). radius=0.3 was run towards HCN only: 7 points, stopping farther from the minimum than the smaller radii.

coordinates¶

Type: list
Default: none stated
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, qchem.ru forum

List of redundant internal coordinates to use, each given as five integers.

About the default: generated automatically.

Value

Meaning

1,i,j,0,0

Distance i–j.

2,i,j,k,0

Angle i–j–k.

3,i,j,k,l

Torsion i–j–k–l.

4,i,j,k,l

Special coordinate for linear fragments. A user describes it as the angle between line l–k and the normal to plane k–j–i.

5,i,j,k,l

Special coordinate for linear fragments (meaning not described).

Note

input.txt spells this keyword coordinated=, which is a typo: version 25 stops with *** error in '$optimize' : unknown name coordinated. Use coordinates=.

See also: fix ($optimize)

fix¶

Type: list
Default: none stated
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, version 25 executable, input.txt, chemport.ru forum, qchem.ru forum, LIMOR page

Internal coordinates to keep fixed during the optimization, in the same five-integer format as coordinates. Several entries are separated by commas or spaces.

Note

Users reported in 2010 that atoms could not be frozen in Cartesian space and that two coordinates could not be constrained to stay equal. This was not checked in version 25, whose executable contains $optimize names of unknown meaning (fragment, weight, local) and restraint groups ($anchor, $confine).

See also: value ($optimize), coordinates ($optimize)

value¶

Type: indexed-array
Default: none stated
Units: Å and degrees
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, input.txt, chemport.ru forum, qchem.ru forum

Values of the fixed internal coordinates. For task=scan, give all the initial values followed by all the final values. val(i)= fills the list starting at position i, so values left unset keep their input-geometry values.

About the default: computed from the input geometry.

Note

Priroda’s dihedral angles have the opposite sign to the convention used by Molden, MOPAC and GAMESS. Flip the sign of any torsion value taken from another program, or the scan starts from a mangled geometry.

Example:

$optimize
 fix   =1,7,9,0,0, 1,8,10,0,0, 3,8,7,9,0, 3,10,9,7,0
 val(1)=1.6,       1.7
 val(5)=2.0,       2.1
 points=5
$end
# 5 optimizations: r(7-9) = 1.6 … 2.0, r(8-10) = 1.7 … 2.1;
# the last two fixed coordinates keep their input values

See also: fix ($optimize), points ($optimize)

gradient¶

Type: switch
Default: none stated
Status: current · not verified
Sources: input.txt

Set gradient=0 when the starting second derivatives were computed with a different method or basis set. This excludes the gradient terms from the internal/Cartesian transformation at the first geometry. Otherwise keep the default.

print¶

Type: switch
Default: none stated
Status: current · not verified
Sources: input.txt

Amount of optimization output.

Value

Meaning

0

Minimal.

1

Detailed

symmetry¶

Type: switch
Default: none stated
Status: undocumented · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: version 25 test runs, version 25 executable, official site files, chemport.ru forum

Keeps point-group symmetry during the optimization (the optimizer switches to Cartesian coordinates); needs $molecule sym= as well. The official 2023–2025 example inputs write it as the prefix sym=1. In version 25, together with $molecule sym=1,0.01, the optimizer switched to Cartesian coordinates (Coordinates: cartesian), printed symmetry: C3v (6) at every step, and returned an exactly symmetric structure followed by MOL> symmetry: C3v. Without $molecule sym=, $optimize sym=1 only switches to Cartesian coordinates and reports symmetry: C1 (1), so give both options.

See also: sym ($molecule)

model¶

Type: integer
Default: none stated
Status: undocumented · not verified
Sources: version 25 executable, official site files

Used as mod=1 with task=opt_n1 (very large systems). In version 25, model is read only by the separate optimizer of task=opt_n1, together with function, h0, delta, fragment, steps, trust, tolerance and print. Meaning not documented.
